subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Simple Gear Trains: In Sequence
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Simple Gear Trains: In Sequence.

hook.text: Line up three gears in a row. The first drives the second, the second drives the third. That's a simple gear train.

buildup.text: The overall ratio depends only on the first and last gears. Middle gears are idlers — they change direction, not ratio.

discovery.text: An idler gear reverses the rotation direction. Add one idler and the output spins the same way as the input.

twist.text: Idlers don't affect speed or torque. They just bridge distance and flip direction. They're mechanical relays.

climax.text: Clock gear trains use many stages to step down mainspring speed to the slow rotation of hour hands.

punchline.text: In a simple train, only the ends matter. The middle just passes the message.

quiz.question: What role do idler gears play in a simple gear train?
options: They multiply torque at each stage of the gear train
They bridge distance and reverse direction without changing the gear ratio
They store energy between gear stages for smoother operation
